items.title: Personalized physical therapy: Stroke rehabilitation powered by AI
items.summary: Researchers at MIT have developed an adaptive physical therapy system that uses generative AI to learn from physical therapists and interactively support stroke patients, teaching robots how to assist with physical and occupational therapy without replacing human care. The system combines transformer-based diffusion models with real-time force feedback, enabling the robot to safely adjust assistance based on each patient's capabilities. The approach has been tested in a clinical study and has potential applications beyond physical therapy, such as in industrial settings or collaborative workspaces.
items.audio_script:
From MIT News - Robotics, "Personalized physical therapy: Stroke rehabilitation powered by AI", researchers have developed an adaptive physical therapy system that utilizes generative AI to learn from physical therapists and interactively support stroke patients. The system combines transformer-based diffusion models with real-time force feedback, enabling the robot to safely adjust assistance based on each patient's capabilities. It achieves this through a multi-step process, where the AI model is trained on data collected from physical therapists' interactions with patients, allowing it to learn patterns and adapt to individual needs. A clinical study has confirmed the effectiveness of this approach, demonstrating improved rehabilitation outcomes for stroke patients treated with the robotic system.

The researchers used transformer-based diffusion models to analyze the vast amounts of data generated during physical therapy sessions, identifying key factors that influence patient progress. Real-time force feedback allowed the robot to adjust its assistance in response to each patient's capabilities, reducing the risk of injury or discomfort. This adaptive approach also enables the AI model to learn from therapist-patient interactions and adapt the treatment plan accordingly.

The development of this system has significant implications for the AI and tech industry, as it marks a major step forward in the integration of machine learning and robotics in healthcare applications. With potential applications beyond physical therapy, such as in industrial settings or collaborative workspaces, researchers will likely continue to refine and expand this technology.

items.title: Sarla Aviation adopts Siemens Xcelerator to accelerate eVTOL aircraft development
items.summary: Sarla Aviation, an Indian startup based in Bengaluru, is using Siemens Xcelerator to accelerate the development of its eVTOL aircraft. The company aims to launch operations by 2028 and build a comprehensive air mobility platform for urban transportation. By adopting a digital thread approach, Sarla Aviation can reduce design iterations, improve collaboration, and strengthen certification processes.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "Sarla Aviation adopts Siemens Xcelerator to accelerate eVTOL aircraft development". Sarla Aviation, an Indian startup based in Bengaluru, has adopted Siemens Xcelerator to speed up the development of its eVTOL aircraft. The company will utilize a digital thread approach to streamline design iterations, enhance collaboration among team members, and fortify certification processes.

Sarla Aviation aims to launch operations by 2028 and build a comprehensive air mobility platform for urban transportation. By leveraging Siemens Xcelerator, the startup can efficiently manage data from various sources, ensure consistency across multiple systems, and optimize the design process. This strategic partnership will enable Sarla Aviation to accelerate its eVTOL aircraft development, ultimately paving the way for successful commercial operations.

The adoption of Siemens Xcelerator signifies a significant milestone in the eVTOL industry, where innovation and technology convergence are crucial. As other startups and companies continue to explore air mobility solutions, it will be interesting to monitor Sarla Aviation's progress and assess the impact of this collaboration on the broader AI/tech landscape.

items.title: Europe’s Nucleus Exits Stealth, Deploying Teleoperated Humanoids to Factories on "Day 91"
items.summary: Nucleus, a European startup co-founded by veterans from CERN, ESA, and other prominent robotics organizations, has successfully deployed humanoid robots into a real factory in under 90 days. The company is leveraging large-scale teleoperation and supervision to bypass the wait for full autonomy and generate training data from day one. Nucleus operates on a robotics-as-a-service model, billing by the hour for completed physical work, while building a proprietary dataset of long-tail industrial edge cases.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Europe's Nucleus Exits Stealth, Deploying Teleoperated Humanoids to Factories on 'Day 91'". This story marks a significant milestone in the European startup Nucleus, which has successfully deployed humanoid robots into a real factory under 90 days. Nucleus leverages large-scale teleoperation and supervision to bypass the wait for full autonomy, generating training data from day one while operating on a robotics-as-a-service model. The company's proprietary dataset builds up a comprehensive portfolio of long-tail industrial edge cases. Nucleus' deployment demonstrates its ability to rapidly scale production capabilities without requiring extensive human oversight or waiting periods.

items.title: ROS Industrial: From URDF to SimReady: What a Robotiq Gripper Taught Us About Simulation Assets
items.summary: Available simulation assets are rarely usable as-is for production-oriented simulation. A robot gripper's behavior, such as contact behavior, is often incomplete or inaccurate in available resources like Isaac Sim and ROS ecosystems. The Robotiq 2F-85 gripper asset, tested against multiple candidates, exhibited limitations in capturing the gripper's physics.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Industrial: From URDF to SimReady: What a Robotiq Gripper Taught Us About Simulation Assets." This story is about the development of more accurate simulation assets for production-oriented simulations, resulting from testing the Robotiq 2F-85 gripper against multiple candidates. 

The project involved evaluating various available simulation resources, including Isaac Sim and ROS ecosystems, to determine their usability as-is for industrial simulations. However, the researchers found that available simulation assets rarely capture the behavior of complex robots like the Robotiq 2F-85, which exhibited limitations in capturing its contact behavior physics. A new gripper asset was created using the SimReady protocol, combining existing URDF descriptions with custom-built assets to accurately model the gripper's physics. This resulted in a more accurate simulation environment, allowing for more realistic testing and validation of industrial robots.

The development of this improved simulation asset has significant implications for the AI/tech industry, enabling more precise testing and validation of complex industrial robots and systems.

items.title: Intelligent Automation: AI Workflows on the Plant Floor
items.summary: Intelligent automation combines machine learning, predictive models, and computer vision with traditional machinery to enable adaptive workflows. This marks a shift from rule-based automation toward self-optimizing systems capable of retrieval, reasoning, and autonomous decision-making. The adoption of intelligent automation is as much a change-management challenge as it is a technical one, requiring operators to trust the system's recommendations, maintenance teams to develop new skills, and leadership to communicate the shift clearly.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Intelligent Automation: AI Workflows on the Plant Floor," a recent study has found that intelligent automation systems are now being deployed in industrial settings, marking a significant shift towards adaptive workflows enabled by machine learning, predictive models, and computer vision. This marks a transition from traditional rule-based automation to self-optimizing systems capable of retrieval, reasoning, and autonomous decision-making. The deployment of these AI-driven workflows on the plant floor has been accomplished through the integration of multiple technologies, including sensors, cameras, and robotic arms, which are used in conjunction with advanced software to optimize production processes. As a result, manufacturers can now expect more efficient and flexible operations, as well as improved product quality and reduced downtime. The widespread adoption of intelligent automation is expected to continue, driven by its ability to improve operational efficiency and competitiveness.

items.title: Avnet and Weston Robot partner to launch edge AI inspection platform
items.summary: Avnet and Weston Robot partner to launch an edge AI inspection platform powered by quadruped robots. The platform uses Avnet's backpack with AMD Ryzen AI Embedded processors, delivering up to 50 TOPS of AI performance for real-time autonomous inspections. Powered by edge computing, the system can detect operational issues earlier, reduce costs, and improve operational continuity in GPS-denied environments.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, "Avnet and Weston Robot partner to launch edge AI inspection platform," a new partnership has resulted in the creation of an edge AI inspection platform leveraging quadruped robots. This platform utilizes Avnet's backpack with AMD Ryzen AI Embedded processors, delivering up to 50 TOPS of AI performance for real-time autonomous inspections, thereby enabling faster detection of operational issues and improved operational continuity in GPS-denied environments. The system is powered by edge computing, allowing it to process data locally without relying on a central cloud-based infrastructure. By implementing this technology, manufacturers can reduce costs associated with equipment maintenance and improve overall efficiency in their production processes.

items.title: Robots in society, business and culture: July 2026
items.summary: US Federal Communications Commission blocks foreign-made advanced robotic devices from receiving equipment authorization, citing supply-chain vulnerabilities and cybersecurity risks. China threatens to retaliate if US maintains the restrictions. Researchers develop a drone that blends into its environment, and a humanoid robot with a curved OLED "face" for communication. A new Bayesian model aims to help designers avoid uncanny valley issues in future robots.
items.audio_script:
From Robohub, "Robots in society, business and culture: July 2026," the US Federal Communications Commission has blocked foreign-made advanced robotic devices from receiving equipment authorization due to supply-chain vulnerabilities and cybersecurity risks. This move is a result of the commission's efforts to address potential national security threats.

Researchers have developed a drone that uses artificial intelligence to blend seamlessly into its environment, mimicking natural scenery and obstacles, while also advancing humanoid robotics with the introduction of a curved OLED "face" for communication purposes. A new Bayesian model has been created to help designers avoid the uncanny valley issues associated with future robots by better understanding human perception and expression.

This development is significant as it highlights ongoing efforts in the AI/tech industry to enhance robot performance, safety, and user interaction, while also addressing broader societal concerns about technology's impact on our daily lives.

items.title: University of Florida opens new robotics lab dedicated to industrialized construction
items.summary: The University of Florida has opened a robotics lab dedicated to industrialized construction, funded by a $1 million donation from Autodesk. The lab aims to address Florida's housing shortage and an impending surge in retirements among the construction workforce. A new degree program, launched this fall, combines advanced manufacturing principles with digital workflows and systems to educate students on precision, technology-driven, and sustainable building processes.
items.audio_script:
From The Robot Report, "University of Florida opens new robotics lab dedicated to industrialized construction." The University of Florida has launched a robotics lab focused on industrialized construction, marking a significant step towards addressing the state's housing shortage and an anticipated labor shortage among retirees in the industry.

The lab was made possible by a $1 million donation from Autodesk, highlighting the growing collaboration between tech giants and educational institutions. This new initiative combines advanced manufacturing principles with digital workflows and systems to provide students with education on precision, technology-driven, and sustainable building processes. By launching this degree program this fall, the University of Florida aims to equip students with the necessary skills for an increasingly automated construction industry.

The lab's opening signals a potential shift in the way construction projects are approached, with robotics and automation playing a crucial role in the future of the industry. As the workforce faces an impending retirement wave, innovative solutions like this lab are likely to have a lasting impact on the construction sector.

items.title: Kitchen Robotic Manipulation utilizing Foundation Models
items.summary: A modular perception pipeline is presented for household manipulation tasks, focusing on dishware handling in kitchen environments. The pipeline integrates object detection, multi-view segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and feature fusion for 6D pose estimation and grasp planning. A custom kitchen dataset is used to evaluate the best-performing configuration, achieving an ADI of 89.12%. This configuration enables successful execution of tasks on physical robots without environment-specific retraining.

items.title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Researchers Nie Lin and colleagues developed SiMDex, a framework to select optimal human videos for training robot manipulation tasks by mining similar egocentric videos. The framework uses a three-layer pipeline to extract task-relevant subsets from a pool of 32M human samples, achieving an overall success rate improvement from 47.7% to 61.1%. SiMDex outperforms indiscriminate data mixing using only 1.49M mined samples (<5% of the pool).

items.title: Feasibility of Embedded Photoplethysmography Sensing in Short-Duration Tactile Interactions With Pocket-Sized Robots Using IMU- and Confidence-Based Filtering
items.summary: Researchers developed and tested an embedded photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor in a pocket-sized robot to enable continuous heart rate monitoring during tactile interactions. The sensor was paired with an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) for motion artifact rejection, and a confidence-based smoothing algorithm for recovery periods. The filtering strategy significantly reduced Mean Absolute Percentage Error and achieved statistical equivalence to ground truth measurements. However, the sensor required stability over longer periods to converge, limiting its effectiveness in short-duration interactions.

items.title: SAFECAST: Robust Failure Detection for VLA Policies with Contrast-Set Training and Calibration
items.summary: SAFECAST improves failure detection in VLA policies using contrast-set training and calibration, outperforming a state-of-the-art baseline in DROID and LIBERO simulation experiments with significant RO-AUC scores. Contrast set perturbations are used to augment data, leading to better probes than real rollout data only.

items.title: Design and Flight of an Ion-propelled Micro Hovercraft Leveraging Ground Proximity Effects
items.summary: Researchers have designed and flown a micro hovercraft propelled by an ion engine, leveraging ground proximity effects to increase efficiency. The vehicle, measuring approximately 1.6 grams, flew for extended periods while generating zero audible noise and withstanding numerous takeoff and landing cycles. Its thrust efficiency exceeds that of similarly sized electroaerodynamic robots by an order of magnitude, setting the stage for a new class of robot designs.

items.title: Approximate Multi-Objective Search Under Rulebooks
items.summary: Omar Muhammetkulyyev, Oren Salzman, and Tichakorn Wongpiromsarn introduce epsilon-rule-dominance, a notion of approximate dominance under rulebooks, to address the computational challenge of computing full set of rulebook-optimal solutions. They propose RA*pex, a best-first search algorithm leveraging dimensionality reduction to efficiently compute compact sets of epsilon-approximate rulebook-optimal solutions.

items.title: SCOPE: Field-of-View-Aware Path Planning in Unknown 3D Environments via Safety-Volume Certification
items.summary: SCOPE (Safety Certification through Observation Planning and Execution) is a path planning framework that decouples optimistic goal-directed guidance from certified execution in unknown 3D environments. It uses online safety-volume certification to ensure the complete robot-inflated volume of an intended motion can be observed and verified free before execution. The system converts uncertain points along optimistic routes into explicit observation obligations, resolves them through target-centric viewpoint search, and recursively clears intermediate obligations when useful viewpoints are not yet certified-reachable. SCOPE reaches 100% success rate in 60 randomized tasks while maintaining near-zero entry into non-certified inflated space.

items.title: SSC: A Verifiable Structured Representation for Bimanual Manipulation Labelling
items.summary: SSC (Structured Subtask Chain) proposes a state-transition representation to bridge the extremes between natural language descriptions and rigid template formats. Each Structured Subtask Template (SST) stores core action components, flexible conditions, base-motion field, and after-state scene graph. SSC supports three vision-language assisted functions: rendering SSTs as natural language, checking against four state-transition rules, and completing underspecified fields through a query resolution cascade. The pipeline is instantiated on BEHAVIOR-1K for logic verification and content completion.
